To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The ground-state phase diagram of a bulk-immiscible binary alloy on a square lattice is characterized by a series of "devils' staircases", i.e., an infinite number of first-order transitions between commensurate, periodic stripe-superstructure phases, and (ii) The average periodicity, or average wavelength, of the ground-state stripe phases is a nonmonotone function of alloy composition.

(i) The ground-state phase diagram of a bulk-immiscible binary alloy film is characterized by an infinite number of ground states, each of them being a commensurate long-period stripe-s superstructure with an average periodicity that varies nonmonotonically with alloy composition.
For a bulk-immiscible binary alloy, the ground-state structure of a thin film is not simply the bulk structure, but rather a superstructure with long-period stripes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of ultrathin alloy superlattice films.

the development of a theoretical framework for the description of epitaxially grown alloy films, which are characterized by a strong coupling between the atomic structure and the electronic properties.
understanding the ground-state phase diagrams of epitaxial alloy thin films.
